name: Optimal trade entry (OTE)
source: 2016 Mentorship: Equilibrium vs Discount / Premium, Framing Low Risk Trade Setups
summary: After a displacement leg in the direction of your higher-timeframe bias, buy the retracement into the 62–79% zone of that leg (70.5% is the sweet spot), ideally where an order block or fair value gap sits.
steps: Higher-timeframe bias and draw on liquidity are clear (where is price going?).
An impulse leg displaces in that direction and the swing is complete (for a high: a lower candle on each side, then a fourth candle lower).
Draw the Fibonacci from the impulse's start to its end. Discount for longs = below 50%; OTE = 62%–79%.
Wait for price to retrace into the OTE zone, ideally into an order block or fair value gap inside it.
Enter at 62–70.5% with a limit order, or on a lower-timeframe shift inside the zone.
entry: Limit order at 62–70.5% of the impulse leg, at the PD array inside the zone.
stop: Beyond the start of the impulse leg (the 100% level).
target: The impulse's high (low for shorts) first, then the next obvious liquidity beyond it.
invalidation: Price trades through the 100% level, or the retracement turns into displacement against you.
checklist: Higher-timeframe bias agrees with the trade direction
The impulse leg displaced and completed a swing
Entry is in the 62–79% zone (discount for longs, premium for shorts)
An order block or FVG sits inside the OTE zone
It's inside the London or New York killzone
Reward is at least 2:1 to the first target
